findings.text: case (3) reads "a JSON file added to a recorded directory leaves the rows unchanged, and an HTML file added to one appears in the next read's rows", but its single control ("drop the build on every moved directory, and the read reads every recorded directory's identity") only falsifies the locality claim; nothing makes the covered-addition claim fail, so the detector path — the source whose job is to decide "whether a covered entry was added, removed or replaced" — could be implemented without ever surfacing an added covered file and still pass this node's gate. Case (2) proves the same claim for the kernel watch with its own second control ("ignore HTML names, and the read returns stale rows"), so the omission is local to case (3).
